dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Now, listen here...

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Huh? You're... I'm sorry, I shouldn't have spoken to you like that. Now, what would you like?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What have you heard?

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: You caught that, eh? Fine. It's nothing important anyway, just stuff you'd hear every day in this tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Like, some people are willing to pay a lot of money to hire some help, while others want to sell certain goods quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Of course, a big shot like you is often mentioned by the guests... But don't you worry! I'm not one to go around telling others your business.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: After all, if you want the details from me, then you have to... Well, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you work here?

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: That's right! I'm a waitre... Ahem, I mean the Chief Mate. Though it's kinda the same job as a waitress...

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: The reason for using titles like this is because Mr. Pitot said it would help with navigating the waves of the business world.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: He said himself that a client from Liyue taught him how to pray for luck by giving auspicious names like this.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: But I reckon... that he didn't quite grasp what they were trying to teach him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bye.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Bye! Hope... hope you have a nice day...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How much Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Mora? Th—That's okay too.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: But if you're using Mora, you'll need to buy more good wine. After all... the information I possess is very valuable. I could sell it for a small fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: However, if you really want to buy "good wine," then please speak with the helmsman. I'll be in trouble if I handle Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If your information is so valuable, why not work for yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: I... I'm afraid of trouble, and working in this tavern is great! Really great. It's safe, comfortable, and there are even free drinks!

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: But most importantly, as long as I'm here then no one will dare come bother me, and I won't be forced to go bother anyone else...

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Anyway, if you really want to buy "good wine," then please speak with the helmsman.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, have you heard anything about me?

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Oh, there have been plenty of stories about you — your adventures, the enemies you've defeated, the treasures you've obtained, and the titles you've earned.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Heck if I know how true they are. Perhaps they're nothing more than drunken ramblings.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: However, if you're interested in these rumors, or if you want to hear some... other stories from me...

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Well... you know.

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Duel

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: What a pity, I seem to have won... But don't lose heart. Perhaps you'd like to take a look at some of our tavern's "good wine"?

dialogues.speaker: Lasselin
dialogues.text: Oh no, I lost! But it was just a game of cards — it doesn't mean I can sell you our special "good wine."
